claims.text: Engineering a controlled distribution of coherent nanoprecipitates in a disordered rare-earth-free high-entropy alloy matrix enhances the low-field magnetocaloric effect.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote efficient magnetic-domain realignment and reduce magnetic hysteresis.
A coherent nanoprecipitate distribution can maintain rapid heat exchange.
A coherent nanoprecipitate distribution can maintain mechanical stability.
Conventionally processed rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys have relatively homogeneous microstructures without tailored precipitate distributions.
Stepwise thermomechanical treatment involving annealing and aging can induce coherent precipitates in a high-entropy alloy.
The proposed treatment will produce a uniform dispersion of coherent precipitates measuring approximately 10–40 nm.
Low applied fields and temperatures near or slightly below room temperature are representative operating conditions for magnetic refrigeration.
Coherent nanoprecipitates facilitate localized magnetic exchange coupling.
Ordered nanoscale structures can provide improved thermal transport in a high-entropy alloy.
Nanoprecipitates act as nucleation centers that lower the energy barrier for magnetic-domain-wall motion.
Lowering the barrier to domain-wall motion reduces hysteresis and enables a larger magnetic entropy change at low fields.
Precipitate coherency keeps the lattice sufficiently connected for rapid heat exchange.
Precipitate coherency preserves mechanical stability.
The treated alloy will exhibit a stronger low-field magnetocaloric response than an identically composed conventionally processed control.
The treated alloy will have lower coercivity than the control.
The treated alloy will maintain or improve thermal conductivity relative to the control.
The treated alloy will maintain or improve mechanical strength relative to the control.
The hypothesis is limited to phase-stable systems capable of forming coherent nanoprecipitates, including some dual bcc/fcc high-entropy alloys.
The proposed effect may fail when secondary incoherent phases predominate or when alloy compositions differ drastically.
